prompt: A promotion can raise revenue and still cost margin. For each promotion that started in 2025 (start_date from 1 January to 31 December 2025), give revenue_uplift, the net revenue on promotion minus the baseline's, and margin_uplift, the gross margin on promotion minus the baseline's. Net revenue is sales.net_revenue_eur, and a line's gross margin is its net_revenue_eur minus units times unit_cost_eur. A sales line is on a promotion when it carries that promotion's ID in order_lines.promo_id, whatever its date; where two promotions overlap on a product, a line carries only the deeper one, so it counts once. The baseline ends the day before the promotion's start_date and has as many days as the promotion ran, start_date and end_date both counted; it holds every sales line of the promotion's products in those days, whatever promotion the line carries. Days are sales.order_date, the UTC day of the order. A period with no sale counts 0. Return three columns, in this order: promo_id, revenue_uplift and margin_uplift. Return one row for each such promotion. Any row order is fine.

output_contract.grain: one row per promotion that started in 2025

hints: Next, write the same-length baseline window, then subtract revenue and margin period from period.
Margin is revenue minus units times unit cost, line by line; add it up in each period before you subtract.
faded_shape:
WITH promo AS (
  -- one row per promotion that started in 2025
  SELECT promo_id, start_date, end_date - start_date + 1 AS days
  FROM promotions
  WHERE start_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-01-01' AND DATE '2025-12-31'
), during AS (
  -- one row per promotion that started in 2025
  SELECT p.promo_id, SUM(s.net_revenue_eur) AS revenue, SUM(s.net_revenue_eur - s.units * s.unit_cost_eur) AS margin
  FROM promo p
  JOIN order_lines ol ON ol.promo_id = p.promo_id
  JOIN sales s ON s.order_line_id = ol.order_line_id
  GROUP BY p.promo_id
), baseline AS (
  -- one row per promotion with a baseline sale
  SELECT p.promo_id, SUM(s.net_revenue_eur) AS revenue, SUM(s.net_revenue_eur - s.units * s.unit_cost_eur) AS margin
  FROM promo p
  JOIN promotion_products pp ON pp.promo_id = p.promo_id
  JOIN sales s ON s.product_id = pp.product_id
why_this_works: Revenue and margin are added up per period on the same lines, so the margin uplift shows what the discount cost.
faded_suffix:
GROUP BY p.promo_id
)
SELECT p.promo_id, COALESCE(d.revenue, 0) - COALESCE(b.revenue, 0) AS revenue_uplift,
  COALESCE(d.margin, 0) - COALESCE(b.margin, 0) AS margin_uplift
FROM promo p
LEFT JOIN during d ON d.promo_id = p.promo_id
LEFT JOIN baseline b ON b.promo_id = p.promo_id
